Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In a directed simple graph with |V| vertices, the maximum number of outgoing edges from any single vertex is |V| − 1, which determines the worst-case cost for a single operation. Using aggregate analysis, the total cost over all |V| operations equals |E|, because each edge is counted exactly once as an outgoing edge of its source vertex.

* (a) The cost of the worst possible single operation is **|V| − 1**, corresponding to a vertex whose out-degree equals the maximum possible (i.e., it has a directed edge to every other vertex in the graph).
* (b) The average amortized cost per operation, computed via aggregate analysis, is **|E| / |V|**, since the aggregate cost of the entire sequence is Σ out(v) = |E| divided across |V| operations.
